title: Switching the active profile is only possible by changing which profile launches at startup
reasoning: The headline capability is genuinely there and correctly wired. ProfileSidebar takes onActivateProfile (profile_sidebar.dart:45), watches activeEquipmentProfileProvider (line 90) and passes activeProfileId down so 'selected' and 'in use' are separate states (an 'IN USE' badge at line 793); the footer shows a primary 'Use This Profile' (line 330, key profileSidebarActivateButtonKey) only when !isActive and demotes Connect All to ButtonVariant.outline there (line 349); the same action heads the popup menu (line 398); every card has a keyed overflow button (line 744). equipment_screen.dart:193 wires it to _activateProfile, which calls equipmentProfilesProvider.setActiveProfile (line 347) — activation only, no isDefault write. So the finding's headline defect is fixed. What does NOT hold is the second half of the claim, that the star was 'relabelled to say what it actually controls'. It still controls more than startup: _setDefaultProfile (equipment_screen.dart:361-385) calls setDefaultProfile(profile.id, makeActive: true), and profiles_provider.dart:1023-1033 routes that through activateProfileStrictTransactional, which pushes the profile into the native executor and makes it active; the remote branch (line 1004, setDefaultProfileRemote) makes it active host-side unconditionally. So after this fix 'Make Startup Default' on a non-active rig still silently switches the rig you are imaging with right now — the exact inverse of the complaint, and worse than a label problem because it re-pushes profile devices to the Rust executor mid-session. The relabel therefore swapped one inaccurate label for a differently inaccurate one rather than making the two actions independent.
evidence: Read all four sites. Ran packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/equipment/profile_sidebar_activate_test.dart: 4/4 green. SEVERED the production wiring three ways in profile_sidebar.dart (footer gate !isActive -> isActive, menu gate !isActive -> isActive, and the card menu key -> null) and re-ran: 3 of 4 went red ('selecting a profile that is not in use offers a way to use it', 'the profile already in use offers no redundant switch', 'every profile card advertises its menu without a right-click'). Restored the file byte-for-byte from a pre-sever copy and re-confirmed lines 329/398/744. The star residual is not covered by any test: no test asserts what onSetDefault does to the active profile. SECOND PASS (this run): repaired the residual. New test profile_startup_default_scope_test.dart passes against the repair; reverting the single argument back to makeActive: true turns it red on exactly the right assertion - 'the star must NOT switch the rig currently in use', Expected: <1> Actual: <2> - and I restored the repaired file byte-for-byte (md5 match against a pre-revert copy). Regression: test/screens/equipment + test/screens/settings together, 615 pass / 5 fail, and all five failures are captures_landscape_test.dart / captures pixel-diff goldens (@Tags(['golden']), host-specific baselines, excluded from `melos run test`); zero RenderFlex overflow anywhere in the log. NOT repaired and NOT repairable here: the REMOTE branch. profiles_provider.dart setDefaultProfile ignores makeActive when a NetworkBackend is the authority - it calls setDefaultProfileRemote, whose own comment says 'makeActive is owned host-side' - so on a phone or tablet paired to a headless host the star still switches the active rig. That is shared core plus a host endpoint, listed in blockedOnSharedCode. I could not exercise the remote path against a real appliance, so that half is read, not run.
repairSummary: equipment_screen.dart _setDefaultProfile now calls setDefaultProfile(profile.id, makeActive: false) instead of true, with the stale comment replaced by one that states the contract. That makes the star mean exactly what its new label says and brings the Equipment screen in line with Settings > Equipment Profiles, whose own handler (equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart:496) has always passed makeActive: false and documents it as 'Pin as the startup default without changing which profile is active' - so the two surfaces no longer disagree about what one label does. New test file packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/equipment/profile_startup_default_scope_test.dart drives the real EquipmentScreen against an in-memory DB with two profiles (A active+default, B selected), long-presses B, taps 'Make Startup Default', and asserts the default moved to B while the ACTIVE profile is still A. It stands in a no-op ProfileSettingsBackend so the pre-fix activation path SUCCEEDS, which makes the revert go red on the real behaviour rather than on an incidental throw.

title: The optical-train step asks the user to look up a pixel size the driver already reports
reasoning: Both halves are in the tree and behave as claimed. (a) camera_step.dart:41-52 computes changedCamera by comparing the live draft cameraId against device.activeDeviceId, matches the driver-reported displayName through hardwarePresetsServiceProvider.matchCameraByName only on a change, and passes preset?.pixelSizeMicrons into OnboardingNotifier.setCamera, whose body (onboarding_provider.dart:198) is pixelSizeMicrons ?? state.pixelSizeMicrons - so re-picking the same camera passes null and a hand-typed value survives, and an unmatched camera prefills nothing. optical_train_step.dart:335 hint now reads "Not in the camera library - check your camera's datasheet" (the old "look this up in your spec sheet" copy is gone) and _pixelSizeProvenance (lines 455-486) renders the attribution line only while the on-screen value still equals the library figure for the matched camera (0.001 um tolerance), so it cannot outlive an edit. Ordering works: OnboardingStep.camera is index 2 and opticalTrain index 7, and _StepBody (onboarding_screen.dart:1146-1177) returns a fresh widget per step, so the optical-train State initState reads the already-seeded draft; the value reaches the created profile at onboarding_screen.dart:426. (b) camera_defaults_step.dart:297-307 leads with a keyed primary "Use <name> settings" button built from the same match, gated on cameraPresetId == null so it retires after apply, and _applyPreset writes only on tap. Residual worth recording, not a defect: the new test covers the seed and the shortcut but NOT the provenance line or the placeholder copy, which is the part the summary says had no test.
evidence: Ran test/screens/onboarding/camera_step_pixel_size_prefill_test.dart + camera_defaults_matched_preset_test.dart: 5/5 green. SEVERED both production call sites at once (camera_step.dart:51 preset?.pixelSizeMicrons -> null, and camera_defaults_step.dart:297 gate -> if (false)) and re-ran: exactly the two behavioural tests went red ("picking a known camera seeds its pixel size", "the camera already chosen is offered by name"). Restored both files from pre-sever copies and re-confirmed lines 51 and 297. Note the second test in the prefill file ("an unrecognised camera prefills nothing") drives setCamera directly rather than the widget, so it survives severing by construction - it is an assertion about the matcher, not about the wiring.

title: The capture-folder step offers no way to type a path
reasoning: The control is real on the LOCAL path and only there. capture_dir_step.dart now renders a keyed TextField (onboardingCaptureDirFieldKey, line 437) with hint 'Type or paste a folder, or use Browse', commits on onSubmitted (line 454) and on focus loss via _onPathFocusChange (line 169), routes through the same onboardingCaptureDirectoryValidatorProvider the picker's result uses, writes the draft only after the check passes and leaves rejected text in the box. Browse is untouched. But the summary's claim that 'Remote mode still asks the host, via the existing _verify path' is where it breaks: in the remote branch _commitTypedPath took `final generation = ++_operationGeneration` and then awaited _verify(path), and _verify's own first act was `final generation = ++_operationGeneration` (line 243). The commit therefore superseded ITSELF, so the very next line, `if (!_isCurrent(generation, authority)) return;`, always fired and the draft write below it was unreachable. On a remote host the operator could type /mnt/host/astro, watch the host confirm it, and the wizard held nothing: no 'Folder is writable.' line (that line is gated on the draft path matching the checked path) and Next still blocked. A second defect rode along: the remote branch cleared _validating BEFORE the round trip, which re-enabled the box, so the disabled-field focus-loss listener re-entered _commitTypedPath and asked the host the identical question a second time - my first test run caught it as validateRemoteDirectory called twice. This is the classic 'works on the path the fixer tested' shape, and it failed on exactly the setup the finding was written about: an appliance driven over VNC runs the app in remote mode.
evidence: The shipped tests (capture_dir_typed_path_test.dart, 3 tests) never leave local mode - no backend override, so isRemoteModeProvider is false in all three. I added packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/onboarding/capture_dir_typed_path_remote_test.dart, which pins backendProvider to a mocktail NetworkBackend (the pattern onboarding_capture_dir_remote_test.dart already uses) and types a path. Against the unrepaired code it failed with `Expected: '/mnt/host/astro' Actual: <null>` on the draft, and the host was asked twice. After the repair all 14 capture-dir tests pass; I re-reverted the one-line fix and confirmed the new test goes red again on the draft assertion, then restored it. Full test/screens/onboarding/ run: 120 pass, 2 fail - captures_landscape_test.dart, which is @Tags(['golden']) with 2026-06-05 host-specific baselines, excluded from `melos run test` and failing at 27-33% pixel diff on Linux font rendering. Pre-existing, and it renders the welcome step, not this one.
repairSummary: capture_dir_step.dart: _verify gained an optional `operation` parameter so a caller that still has work to do after the check can share its generation instead of superseding itself; the remote branch of _commitTypedPath now calls `_verify(path, operation: generation)`, keeps _validating set for the whole round trip (which keeps the box disabled and stops the focus-loss listener firing a duplicate host query), and additionally requires _checkedPath == path before writing the draft. Local behaviour is byte-identical. New test file capture_dir_typed_path_remote_test.dart covers accept and reject on the host, and asserts exactly one round trip.

title: Equipment Settings mixes auto-save and Apply-required sections and repeats its own title
reasoning: (a) holds: settings_tab.dart:36-55 renders the card grid with no in-content heading, and both hosts do supply one - equipment_screen.dart:719 (phone AppBar) and :736 (SkotiqDialog title), both from l10n key equipmentSettingsTitle. (b) is built as described - Apply is gated on `_initialized && !_saving && _hasPendingEdits` (line 692), a warning-toned keyed line 'Not applied yet - press Apply to send these to the guider.' renders above the existing 'Last applied:' line (lines 757-776), and the section blurb states the contract (line 745). But the summary's closing claim - 'Typing a value back to its stored value clears the pending state, so the warning never cries wolf' - was false for five of the eight fields. _hasPendingEdits compared controller TEXT against `value.toString()`. Three of the eight values are doubles (exposureSecs, minPulseMs, maxPulseMs), so typing 1500 into Max Pulse and pressing Apply stored 1500.0, whose toString() is '1500.0' and never again equals the '1500' in the box: after a SUCCESSFUL apply the card went on warning 'Not applied yet' about a value the guider was already running, with Apply live to re-send it, for the rest of the session. The int fields had the milder version of the same thing (a leading zero, '0111' vs '111'). That is precisely the cry-wolf the fix set out to prevent, relocated from 'Apply looks the same either way' to 'the warning is permanently on'.
evidence: The shipped test file drives ONE field, gain - an int, and only with clean text ('333', '111'), which is why the double case was never seen. I added two cases to equipment_settings_pending_edits_test.dart: max pulse typed as '1500' then applied, and gain typed as '0111'. Both failed against the unrepaired code (Expected: false, Actual: <true> on the Apply enablement) and pass after the repair; 6/6 now green. SEVERED the wiring (Apply's onPressed no longer consulting _hasPendingEdits, and the pending Text gated to `if (false)`) and all 6 went red, so the tests are attached to the production gate, not to the getter in isolation. Restored settings_tab.dart from a pre-sever copy. Full test/screens/equipment/ run afterwards: 157 pass, 3 fail - captures_landscape_test.dart only, which is @Tags(['golden']) with host-specific baselines (21-27% pixel diff, no RenderFlex overflow anywhere in the log), excluded from `melos run test`. I looked specifically for the Row-overflow regression shape given the new '...' button on the profile cards: no overflow exception at 640x360, 430x932 or 932x430.
repairSummary: settings_tab.dart: _hasPendingEdits now compares each field to the running config NUMERICALLY via a new _differsNum(controller, applied) helper (num.tryParse of the trimmed text; unparseable text counts as pending, which is what half-typed input is), replacing the eight text != value.toString() comparisons. Two regression tests added to equipment_settings_pending_edits_test.dart covering a decimal field and a leading zero.

title: INDI and Alpaca startup discovery default to off after the wizard offered them as scan backends
reasoning: The code is there and the wiring reaches the surface the finding named. onboarding_provider.dart:502 _persistAppSettings is called from complete() (line 474), the only caller of complete() in the tree (onboarding_screen.dart:339). Local branch (lines 533-539) writes 'indi_auto_connect' and 'alpaca_auto_discover' through settingsDao.setSettings; those are the exact keys default_settings.dart:50/53 seeds to 'false', that app_settings_stored_snapshot_mapping.dart:151/155 reads into AppSettings, and that connection_settings.dart:188/220 renders as the 'Query INDI/Alpaca on startup' switches - the same two the finding said asked the question a second time. Remote branch (lines 519-529) is a genuine read-modify-write: getSettings() returns the whole AppSettings (imaging_profile_operations.dart:96) and updateSettings POSTs settings.toJson() whole, so nothing the copyWith did not carry is dropped. Both flags are written unconditionally when hasDrivers, so unticking INDI takes an inherited true away (test 2 proves it), and hasDrivers==false leaves both alone (test 3). I checked the four ways this could have been hollow and none of them are: (i) the master gate auto_discover_on_launch defaults 'true' (default_settings.dart:13), so a true indiAutoConnect actually reaches auto_discovery_launcher.dart:108 at launch rather than dying behind an off switch; (ii) dao.setSettings is a per-key upsert batch, so it cannot clobber the image_output_path written just above; (iii) the wizard has no INDI/Alpaca host field at all (grep of screens/onboarding for indiServerHost is empty), so persisting the flag without an address is not leaving half the answer behind - both wizard scan and startup scan use the same localhost defaults; (iv) discoveryBackendsForPolicy filters the backend list before the scan, so the flags genuinely gate which backends run. Honest residual, not a defect: the driver step pre-ticks every non-simulator backend (onboarding_provider.dart:119-125), so an operator who clicks through now ships with INDI and Alpaca startup queries ON where they were OFF before. I judged that the intended reading of the finding rather than an inversion - the step's copy is 'Pick everything that applies to your setup', the cost of a wrong true is one failed localhost:7624 connect and one UDP broadcast in a fire-and-forget background task, and settings.autoDiscoverOnLaunch was already true so the scan was happening regardless.
evidence: Read onboarding_provider.dart:498-544, the DAO, both mapping files, the launcher and driver_step.dart. Baseline test/providers/onboarding_discovery_backends_test.dart: 3/3 green. SEVERED the production call site (the `if (hasDrivers)` guard around dao.setSettings -> `if (false)`) and re-ran: 2 of 3 went red ('the backends ticked in the wizard are queried at startup', 'unticking a backend turns its startup query back off'); the third ('a draft with no driver answer leaves the toggles alone') survives by construction because it asserts nothing is written. Restored onboarding_provider.dart from a pre-sever copy and re-confirmed hasDrivers at lines 512/526/527/535. Regression: all three skotiq_core onboarding test files together (onboarding_provider_test, onboarding_cool_on_connect_test, onboarding_discovery_backends_test) 24/24 green. Not verifiable without a paired appliance: the remote branch has no test - I read it rather than ran it.

title: Discovery says only that no switches or cover calibrators were found, without saying why or what to do
reasoning: The code is there and it is the cause-level fix, not a relocation. discovery_panel.dart:647 sets isEmpty inside _buildDeviceGroupSection, the ONE helper all eleven device-class sections go through (call sites at lines 524-614), so there is no class left on the old path - I checked for the 'third copy of the bug' shape and there is only one discovery surface in the tree: nothing else in packages/skotiq_app/lib, apps/mobile or apps/desktop renders a device-class list, and the only two matches for 'No switches found' anywhere are the two comments in this file describing what was removed. Empty classes keep the titled header, the icon, an honest '${devices.length} found' (line 690) and gain a rescan IconButton (line 696); _buildEmptyClassBody (line 731) names the backends from discoveryState.backendStates and marks the failures from errorBackends, or says 'Not searched yet - run a scan.' before the first scan. I checked the two ways this line could have been a NEW false claim rather than a fix for an old one: (i) backendStates is rebuilt from scratch by discoverAll (_discoveringStateForBackends with mergeWithExisting: false, provider line 61), and the list it is built from is discoveryBackendsForPolicy(...) - the post-filter set - so 'Searched: X, Y' names the backends that actually ran, not the ones that were available; (ii) 'Settings -> Connection' is the real route: connection_settings.dart:70 is titled 'Connection' and carries the INDI and Alpaca server host/port fields. The rescan button re-entering during a scan is covered by _scanForDevices's own `if (_isScanning || _isRescanning) return` guard (line 175). Honest residual, judged not a regression from this fix: the new IconButton measures 32x32 at 360dp, under the 48dp bar mobile_tap_target_test.dart enforces elsewhere - but its immediate neighbour, the pre-existing header rescan button, is explicitly minimumSize: Size(32,32) with tapTargetSize.shrinkWrap (lines 390-392), so the new control follows the file's established size rather than introducing a new violation, and the tap-target suite never reaches either because the panel is collapsed by default.
evidence: Read discovery_panel.dart:633-775, unified_discovery_provider.dart discoverAll/_discoveringStateForBackends/_getAvailableBackends, and discovery_state.dart errorBackends. Baseline discovery_empty_class_section_test.dart: 2/2 green. SEVERED the production wiring (early-returned the old bare italic 'No <class> found' Text from _buildDeviceGroupSection whenever isEmpty) and BOTH tests went red; restored discovery_panel.dart and confirmed md5-identical to a pre-sever copy. I then measured the new IconButton by instrumenting a pump at 360dp: Size(32.0, 32.0). GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (test-only, no production change): the fix's own comment claims it repaired a 24px overflow of the header Row at 360dp, but every test in the file ran at 1280 where it fitted either way - the overflow repair was untested. I added 'the empty-class section fits a 360dp phone' to discovery_empty_class_section_test.dart, which expands the panel by tapping the header (below the phone breakpoint the header drops its 'Expand' label) and asserts takeException() is null plus the chrome renders. It passes; reverting the `Expanded` around the title back to a bare Text + Spacer makes it fail with 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 24 pixels on the right' - the exact number the comment claims - and I restored the file md5-identical afterwards. Regression: test/screens/equipment + test/screens/settings, 615 pass / 5 fail, all five golden pixel-diffs (@Tags(['golden'])), zero overflow exceptions. dart format and dart analyze clean on the edited test.
